subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw expose a cross-channel Gateway receipt timestamp to agents, and if so what field name, trust block, and timestamp format should become the stable contract?
rationale: The missing field is source-proven, but the fix would create durable agent-visible metadata and shared plugin/channel SDK surface, so automation should not choose the public contract unilaterally.

options.title: Add a generic receipt timestamp
options.body: Expose one cross-channel field such as `gatewayReceivedAt` in the chosen metadata block and carry it through SDK/channel ingress with tests for at least one durable and one direct path.

options.title: Keep timing in diagnostics only
options.body: Avoid agent-visible metadata and solve latency attribution through Gateway/channel stage logs or trace events instead.

options.title: Leave timing to plugins
options.body: Let each channel expose receipt timing independently, accepting inconsistent field names and weaker cross-channel comparability.

recommendation.title: Add a generic receipt timestamp
recommendation.body: Expose one cross-channel field such as `gatewayReceivedAt` in the chosen metadata block and carry it through SDK/channel ingress with tests for at least one durable and one direct path.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current routing candidate from the central envelope/prompt metadata history and prior adjacent timestamp review context.
